cohort: The study included mothers admitted to a tertiary hospital's intensive care unit, with cases being 198 patients diagnosed with Maternal Near-Miss between 2018-2022, and controls being mothers who gave birth in the same hospital in 2023 without puerperal complications.
finding: Co-morbidities were 5.5 times more frequent in patients diagnosed with MNM compared to the control group, and unexpectedly, education level and family income were found to be higher in the MNM group.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was identified as a reason for intensive care unit admission in 10.10% of Maternal Near-Miss cases.
